clue.text: I would suggest Adam, oddly enough

definitions.meaning: the pronoun I is the grammatical form a speaker uses for themself alone
Adam was the first man created, and alone, single

explanation.surface: Someone proposes the name Adam for no obvious reason.
explanation.walkthrough: The grammar term for the pronoun 'I' also describes Adam, the first human, who was for a time the only one, hence 'oddly enough'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammarians call the pronoun of a lone speaker by this term, and Genesis makes Adam the original, solitary human.

clue.text: Whimsical person a theologian takes in hand

indicators.note: the hand closes round the following words, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a fist is a closed hand
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A churchman grasps something in his hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' puts A and DD inside FIST, giving F-ADD-IST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows passing crazes on a whim is a crank for fashions of the moment.

clue.text: Injuries arising from haymaking

definitions.meaning: sprains or wrenches of a joint
hayricks are the stacks built when hay is made

explanation.surface: Farm workers hurt themselves bringing in the hay.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrenched joint is a sprain; stacks of hay built in the field are the other sense.

clue.text: Salesman, perhaps, going places

definitions.meaning: a commercial rep who travels a sales territory is one example
one who goes from place to place is on a journey

explanation.surface: A rep on the road between appointments.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial rep on the road is called this, and anyone making a journey is one too.

clue.text: Leave by the door

parts.note: the word for departing is also the sign marking the doorway out

explanation.definitionFit: To depart a room through its door is to go out, and the door itself is labelled the way out.

clue.text: See 1
Dapper as a prohibitionist in New York

indicators.note: the prohibitionist sits within the city's abbreviation

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed temperance campaigner in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places A TT within NY, giving N-ATT-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone smart and neatly turned out.

clue.text: Simply grand style of dress for exercise

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: a new style refashions the letters before it into another shape

explanation.surface: Praise for an elegant outfit worn to the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style of' reworks SIMPLY plus G. A gymslip is a sleeveless tunic once worn by British schoolgirls for PE.
explanation.definitionFit: This sleeveless tunic was the standard garment for school physical education lessons.

clue.text: Made another mess of something she heard about

indicators.note: the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A gossip garbles something she overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SHE HEARD. A hash is a mess, so rehashing is making another one from old material.
explanation.definitionFit: To rework old material into a new jumble is to serve up the same hash again.

clue.text: Command of words stenographers cope with

definitions.meaning: a stenographer takes down words read out to them

explanation.surface: Typists struggle to keep up with spoken orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying down orders authoritatively is dictating, and text read aloud for a secretary to transcribe is the other sense.

clue.text: Unit the Royal Marines

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A detachment of British naval commandos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' looks military; it is a measure of heat, a therm being 100,000 British thermal units used on UK gas bills.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a measure of heat energy once used to bill British gas supply.

clue.text: Having grown out of, falls into disuse

indicators.note: the word collapses into a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Something outgrown is no longer used.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has emerged from a source has come forth or descended from it.

clue.text: Reveille?

parts.note: the bugle at dawn summons soldiers to their work

explanation.definitionFit: The morning bugle call rouses troops to report for their obligations.

clue.text: Somehow lets us struggle

indicators.note: the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.definitionFit: A scuffle or vigorous fight is another word for a struggle.

clue.text: Material that sounds suitable ta for a dunce's hat

indicators.note: the phrase is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.words: suitable ta for a dunce's hat
parts.note: a dunce's cap was a cone, fit for someone silly, so a silly cone; 'ta' is a stray OCR mark

explanation.surface: Choosing fabric for a pointed classroom punishment cap.
explanation.walkthrough: Dunces were once made to wear a cone-shaped paper hat, a silly cone.
explanation.definitionFit: This synthetic polymer is used as a sealant, rubber and lubricant.

clue.text: Privation suffered in the early days of sail?

definitions.text: Privation suffered in the early days of sail?

parts.words: Privation suffered in the early days of sail?
parts.note: read as two words, a tough vessel; read as one, misfortune

explanation.definitionFit: Suffering from want or adversity is a privation, and early sailing vessels were tough on board.

clue.text: Not where plate-layers are trained for service

definitions.text: Not where plate-layers are trained for service

parts.words: Not where plate-layers are trained for service
parts.note: plate-layers are track workers, but here they are people setting plates on a train

explanation.definitionFit: This railway carriage is where meals are served to passengers on board.

clue.text: Flower giving incentive to a w bit of fun

indicators.note: the incentive is added on to the bit of fun

parts.note: a lark is a piece of fun; the 'w' is a stray OCR mark
a spur is a goad or incentive

explanation.surface: A bunch of blooms as encouragement for some mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphinium-like garden plants with spurred blue blossoms go by this name.

clue.text: Plant that gets Virginia in real trouble

parts.note: VA is the US state abbreviation for Virginia

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A herb causes problems for an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges IN REAL into LERIAN, after VA.
explanation.definitionFit: This herb has a root used as a sedative.

clue.text: Sensational turn of English with little right in a Spanish port

indicators.note: the pieces sit within the port's name

parts.note: Vigo is a port in Galicia, Spain
RT is a short form of right

explanation.surface: A dizzy moment for an Englishman in a Spanish harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E and RT inside VIGO: V-ERT-IGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizziness is a feeling of the world spinning round.

clue.text: Current conductors circulating in a mountain range

indicators.note: the round letter sits within the range

parts.note: the Andes is South America's mountain range
something circling makes a circle, the letter O

explanation.surface: Electric cables run around a stretch of mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the circle O within ANDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrodes through which electric current flows into a device are these.

clue.text: Too many lampreys for St Henry I?

definitions.text: Too many lampreys for St Henry I?

parts.words: Too many lampreys for St Henry I?
parts.note: Henry I of England is said to have died from eating too many lamprey eels

explanation.definitionFit: An excess, the word used in the tale of the king's fatal meal of eels.

clue.text: Gibraltar tea-time offering?

parts.note: Gibraltar is known as the Rock, so a teatime bake from there

explanation.definitionFit: A small rough-surfaced fruit bun eaten at tea in Britain.

clue.text: Ship's complement including a Cavalier poet

indicators.note: the crew contains the single letter

parts.note: a ship's complement is its crew

explanation.surface: A Royalist poet is among those aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Carew was one of the Cavalier poets, Royalists under Charles I.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carew wrote lyrics at the court of Charles I among the Royalist versifiers.

clue.text: He shoots a bird right in the tail

indicators.note: the letter comes at the end, the tail of the bird

parts.note: a snipe is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A hunter hits a bird in its tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman firing from cover is a hidden gunman.

clue.text: Fruit crop

explanation.definitionFit: A dried plum is one sense; cutting back growth is the other.

clue.text: Stinging riposte shows under-ti standing

indicators.note: the letters are on show inside the clue words

explanation.walkthrough: The definition prints as 'under-ti standing' with stray OCR letters 'ti'; it reads 'understanding'. 'shows' signals the run on show across 'stinging riposte'.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm grasp of a subject is comprehension of it.

clue.text: This man has stomach

parts.note: the phrase 'the ___ man' means a person's appetite or stomach

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for one's appetite, 'the ___ man', refers to the belly.

clue.text: It makes a downfall look graceful

definitions.text: It makes a downfall look graceful

parts.words: It makes a downfall look graceful
parts.note: a literal fall from an aircraft made gentle by a canopy

explanation.definitionFit: A canopy that slows a descent from an aircraft.

clue.text: All right in part

parts.note: an actor who has all the lines of a role correct

explanation.definitionFit: An actor who knows every line of a role exactly.
